answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent's reputation to a single, costly identity: before earning, an agent posts a refundable bond tied to one long-lived key, and every completed job adds verifiable work history that cannot be copied to a fresh identity. An auditor that only mirrors past performance, counting jobs rather than claims, would treat a new clone like a raven arriving with no track record: a stranger. Splitting one bonded history across many identities dilutes reputation and wastes the bond, making mass fakery expensive and pointless.
